Title: Empagliflozin in Heart Failure with a Preserved Ejection Fraction
Population: Adults with symptomatic NYHA class II–IV heart failure and LVEF >40%.
Primary endpoints: First cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure
Interpretation: The primary composite outcome favored empagliflozin, driven mainly by fewer heart-failure hospitalizations. A significant reduction in cardiovascular mortality alone was not established.

Title: Dapagliflozin in Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction
Population: Adults with symptomatic heart failure and LVEF >40%, including some with previously reduced EF that had improved.
Primary endpoints: First worsening heart failure (hospitalization or urgent visit) or cardiovascular death
Interpretation: Dapagliflozin lowered the risk of the primary composite of worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death. Cardiovascular death alone did not show a statistically clear reduction.

Title: Angiotensin-Neprilysin Inhibition in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction
Population: Patients with NYHA class II–IV heart failure, LVEF ≥45%, elevated natriuretic peptides, and structural heart disease.
Primary endpoints: Total heart-failure hospitalizations and cardiovascular death
Primary endpoint results: 894 vs 1,009 total primary events; rate ratio 0.87 (95% CI 0.75–1.01), p=0.06.
Interpretation: The prespecified primary composite did not meet statistical significance in the overall study population.

Title: Spironolactone for Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction
Population: Patients with symptomatic heart failure and LVEF ≥45%.
Primary endpoints: Cardiovascular death, aborted cardiac arrest, or HF hospitalization
Primary endpoint results: 18.6% (spironolactone) vs 20.4% (placebo); HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.77–1.04), p=0.14.
Interpretation: No statistically significant reduction in the primary composite; hospitalization for heart failure alone was lower, while hyperkalemia was more frequent.

Title: Semaglutide in Patients with Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction and Obesity
Population: Patients with HFpEF and obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m²); LVEF ≥45% under the trial eligibility criteria.
Primary endpoints: Change in KCCQ clinical summary score at 52 weeks | Percentage change in body weight at 52 weeks
Primary endpoint results: Mean change +16.6 vs +8.7 points; estimated difference +7.8 points (95% CI 4.8–10.9), p<0.001. | Mean change −13.3% vs −2.6%; difference −10.7 percentage points (95% CI −11.9 to −9.4), p<0.001.
Interpretation: Semaglutide improved patient-reported symptoms/physical limitations and reduced weight in obesity-associated HFpEF. This trial was not primarily designed to establish mortality benefit.

Title: Finerenone in Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction
Population: Patients with symptomatic heart failure and LVEF ≥40%.
Primary endpoints: Total worsening HF events and cardiovascular death
Primary endpoint results: 1,083 vs 1,283 total primary events; rate ratio 0.84 (95% CI 0.74–0.95), p=0.007.
Interpretation: Finerenone reduced the rate of the recurrent-event composite outcome. Hyperkalemia occurred more often; cardiovascular death considered alone was not significantly reduced.

Title: Effects of candesartan in patients with chronic heart failure and preserved left-ventricular ejection fraction
Population: Patients with chronic symptomatic HF and EF >40%.
Primary endpoint results: Unadjusted HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.77–1.03), p=0.118; fewer CHF admissions observed.
Interpretation: Overall unadjusted primary composite did not reach significance; admissions for HF were lower.

Title: Irbesartan in patients with heart failure and preserved ejection fraction
Population: Symptomatic HF in adults aged at least 60 years.
Primary endpoint results: Primary outcome HR 0.95 (95% CI 0.86–1.05), p=0.35; not significant.
Interpretation: Irbesartan did not significantly reduce the prespecified clinical composite.

Title: The perindopril in elderly people with chronic heart failure (PEP-CHF) study
Population: Older adults with HF, echocardiographic suggestion of diastolic dysfunction, and no substantial LV systolic dysfunction.
LVEF eligibility: Not specified as a numerical EF threshold in the abstract
Primary endpoints: All-cause mortality or unplanned HF hospitalization
Primary endpoint results: HR 0.919 (95% CI 0.700–1.208), p=0.545; trial was underpowered.
Interpretation: No significant primary outcome difference; under-enrollment and crossover to open-label ACE inhibitors limit interpretation.

Title: Effect of phosphodiesterase-5 inhibition on exercise capacity and clinical status in HFpEF
Population: Symptomatic HFpEF with objective evidence of elevated filling pressure and reduced exercise capacity.
Primary endpoint results: No significant improvement in peak oxygen consumption with sildenafil.
Interpretation: Sildenafil did not improve exercise capacity or clinical status in the overall HFpEF study population.

Title: Effect of spironolactone on diastolic function and exercise capacity in patients with HFpEF
Population: Ambulatory HFpEF patients with preserved EF and diastolic dysfunction.
Primary endpoints: E/e′, diastolic function | Peak oxygen consumption
Primary endpoint results: Adjusted between-group E/e′ difference −1.5 (95% CI −2.0 to −0.9); p<0.001. | No significant improvement in exercise capacity.
Interpretation: Improved echocardiographic diastolic function without improving peak oxygen consumption.

Title: Isosorbide Mononitrate in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction
Population: HFpEF patients in a crossover study with daily activity tracking.
Primary endpoint results: No beneficial increase in daily activity; activity tended to be lower with isosorbide mononitrate.
Interpretation: Isosorbide mononitrate did not improve daily activity.

Title: The angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor LCZ696 in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
Population: Symptomatic NYHA II–III HF with EF ≥45% and NT-proBNP >400 pg/mL.
Primary endpoint results: The phase 2 trial found a greater short-term decrease in NT-proBNP with LCZ696 versus valsartan.
Interpretation: A biomarker-focused phase 2 trial; not evidence of a confirmed reduction in HF hospitalization or mortality.

Title: Effect of Sacubitril/Valsartan vs Standard Medical Therapies on NT-proBNP and Exercise Capacity
Comparator: Enalapril, valsartan, or placebo according to prior therapy
Population: Symptomatic HF with EF >40%, structural heart disease, elevated NT-proBNP and reduced quality of life.
Primary endpoint results: Adjusted geometric mean ratio 0.84 (95% CI 0.80–0.88), p<0.001. | Adjusted mean difference −2.5 m (95% CI −8.5 to 3.5), p=0.42.
Interpretation: NT-proBNP improved, but the co-primary 6-minute walk endpoint did not.

Title: Effect of empagliflozin on exercise ability and symptoms in HF with preserved EF
Population: HF with EF >40%, with or without type 2 diabetes.
Primary endpoint results: Between-group median difference 4.0 m (95% CI −5.0 to 13.0), p=0.37.
Interpretation: No significant improvement in 6-minute walk distance; this paper also reports the separate EMPERIAL-Reduced study.

Title: The SGLT2 inhibitor dapagliflozin in HFpEF: a multicenter randomized trial
Population: Symptomatic HFpEF with patient-reported health-status limitation.
Primary endpoint results: Between-group treatment difference +5.8 points (95% CI 2.3–9.2), p=0.001.
Interpretation: Dapagliflozin improved KCCQ clinical summary score over 12 weeks.

Title: Vericiguat in patients with worsening chronic HF and preserved EF
Population: Recently worsening symptomatic HF, EF ≥45%.
Primary endpoint results: No significant difference in log NT-proBNP between pooled vericiguat dose arms and placebo. | No significant difference in left atrial volume between pooled vericiguat dose arms and placebo.
Interpretation: The trial did not meet either co-primary endpoint; quality-of-life signals were exploratory.

Title: Atrial shunt device for HF with preserved and mildly reduced EF
Population: Selected HF patients with elevated exercise pulmonary capillary wedge pressure; 626 randomized.
Outcome categories: Cardiovascular events; HF hospitalization; Symptoms/quality of life
Interpretation: No improvement in the overall hierarchical composite compared with sham.

Title: Semaglutide in Patients with Obesity-Related HFpEF and Type 2 Diabetes
Population: Obesity-related HFpEF with BMI ≥30 kg/m² and type 2 diabetes.
Primary endpoints: KCCQ Clinical Summary Score | Body weight
Primary endpoint results: Between-group difference +7.3 points (95% CI 4.1–10.4), p<0.001. | Difference −6.4 percentage points (95% CI −7.6 to −5.2), p<0.001.
Interpretation: Both symptom and weight co-primary endpoints favored semaglutide.

Title: Tirzepatide for Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction and Obesity
Population: HFpEF (EF ≥50%) with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m²).
Outcome categories: Cardiovascular events; HF hospitalization; Symptoms/quality of life
Primary endpoints: CV death or worsening HF event | KCCQ Clinical Summary Score
Primary endpoint results: HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.41–0.95), p=0.026. | Between-group difference +6.9 points (95% CI 3.3–10.6), p<0.001.
Interpretation: Both co-primary outcomes favored tirzepatide; the primary event difference should not be interpreted as a separate CV death benefit.

Title: Effect of Caloric Restriction or Aerobic Exercise Training on Peak Oxygen Consumption and Quality of Life
Population: Older adults with obesity and stable HFpEF.
Primary endpoint results: Aerobic exercise and caloric restriction each improved peak oxygen consumption in a 2×2 factorial design.
Interpretation: Lifestyle arms improved exercise capacity; the factorial design differs from two-arm medication RCTs.

Title: Effect of Vericiguat vs Placebo on Quality of Life in Patients With HFpEF
Population: Symptomatic HFpEF after recent worsening HF.
Primary endpoint results: 15-mg vs placebo difference −1.5 points (95% CI −5.5 to 2.5), p=0.47.
Interpretation: No significant difference in the primary KCCQ physical limitation outcome at 24 weeks.
